planner.question: Can direct DAG restriction charging replace exponential formula unfolding and yield a valid general circuit lower-bound measure?
planner.strategy: Count distinct entering wires of each block-dependent sub-DAG and sum physical gate support differences.
planner.alternative: Build an explicit indirect-storage-access circuit with superlinear summed log residual counts and linear gate size.
planner.stop_rule: Do not convert a superlinear aggregate charge into physical gate count without a justified per-gate bound.
literature_leads: Prior MathOS guarded selector restrictions; elementary subfunction counting and indirect storage access. No novelty claim.

construct.claim: For arbitrary binary circuits, sum log2 residual counts <= sum boundary wires <= J(C); the universal SAT selector has J(C)>=t*m=Omega(N^(4/3)/log N).
construct.scope: Single-output binary DAG, disjoint input blocks present at output, syntactic support, output ancestor cone.
construct.derivation: Fix outside inputs, record incoming cut values, evaluate dependent DAG; count each gate incidence by support symmetric difference.
unresolved_steps: Independent universal control on per-gate charges for SAT or a stronger semantic measure.
candidate_tests: All three-gate truth-function assignments on two skeletons and every block restriction.

alternative.claim: Indirect storage access has sum log residual counts k^2 but 3(l+1)(k-1) gates, refuting universal linear charging of exact subfunction counts.
alternative.scope: k=2^l pointer blocks of l bits, one primary address and k-bit data table, binary gate mux trees.
alternative.derivation: Select pointer block i and arbitrary data table to realize every function on that block; shared selection circuits are linear in input length.
unresolved_steps: A noncircular property separating SAT from compact shared selection circuitry.
candidate_tests: Construct mux DAGs and verify every small pointer and table configuration; count structural charges.

objections: One gate can be charged to many blocks.

counterexample_candidates: Indirect storage access realizes k^2 summed log residuals with O(k log k) gates.
